Switzerland's AI should answer in Romansh too, not just German, French and Italian, so the smaller language communities aren't left behind.
Any AI used by federal or cantonal offices should explain in plain language why it made a decision that affects me, and let me contest it.
Build the national AI so my health and tax data never leaves Swiss servers, and is never used to train models without my explicit consent.
Give every school a free, vetted AI tutor that also works offline, so kids in rural cantons get the same help as those in Zurich.
Cantons, not only the federal government, should decide how AI is used in their own public services, the way we already do with schools and police.
The national AI should stay politically neutral on contested votes and just lay out what each side argues, rather than nudging people one way.
Use AI to cut the paperwork for permits and benefits, but always keep a real person I can reach when the system gets it wrong.
Publish the AI's training-data sources and error rates openly, so researchers and citizens can audit it the way we audit public accounts.
Let people shape the rules for the national AI through the popular-initiative system, so its charter stays under democratic control.
The AI should help doctors in small clinics catch rare conditions earlier, but the doctor, not the model, always makes the final call.
